summary: Organize, name and keep far larger results, see what is slowing your server with the rest of Activity Monitor, and pick up where you left off with restored connections.

changes.title: Results as tabs
changes.text: Show one result at a time with a row of result tabs, each with its own Table and Pivot view, or switch back to Stacked. Go to Result (Ctrl+Shift+O) lists every result, Pivot and comparison with a filter, and Ctrl+Page Up/Down, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 and Ctrl+Alt+Page Up/Down move between results. Each result's close button frees just that result.

changes.title: Named results
changes.text: Put /* #Name="Open orders" */ or -- #Name="Open orders" before a statement to name its result. The name appears on its tab and caption, in Go to Result, Compare, Pivot titles and suggested Save Results As file names. The query runs exactly as written; where Varia cannot tell which result a statement returns, the Messages tab explains why the name was not applied.

changes.title: Pivots that belong to their result
changes.text: Each result owns one Pivot, drawn beneath it. Building again replaces it in place without losing focus or column widths. When you change a result's filters, its Pivot shows Out of date with Update, and small, quick Pivots rebuild by themselves.

changes.title: Compare popover and Keep Selected Rows
changes.text: Compare opens a small popover beside the grid to choose the other result, swap old and new and compare exact text. Keep Selected Rows filters a grid to the rows you selected, as one removable filter.

changes.title: Progress and Cancel for long result operations
changes.text: Slow sorts, filters, profiles, Pivots and comparisons show their phase and percentage with Cancel in the results toolbar. Cancel or Escape keeps the grid's previous order and rows.

changes.title: Discard results after execution
changes.text: As in SSMS, run a query without keeping its rows, for timing very large queries. Plans and client statistics are still collected, and the status bar and the empty grid say that results were discarded, with a way to turn it off and run again.

changes.title: Activity Monitor, complete
changes.text: Blocking, Active Expensive Queries, Recent Expensive Queries, Resource Waits and Data File I/O join the Sessions grid, which now uses the results grid's sorting and filters. Right-click a session for Details (statement, waits, transactions, tempdb use and locks) or Kill Process, which asks first and explains rollback.

changes.title: Table Properties
changes.text: Open SSMS's Table Properties from Object Explorer or Peek: General, Permissions, Change Tracking, Storage, Security Predicates and Extended Properties. Lock escalation, change tracking and extended properties apply in one transaction, and Script shows the same statements.

changes.title: View Dependencies and Go To Definition
changes.text: View Dependencies shows what depends on an object, or what it depends on, as a tree read as you expand it. In a query, F12 scripts the object under the caret as CREATE to a new tab, Alt+F12 opens it in Peek, and Ctrl+click follows F12.

changes.title: Connections that come back
changes.text: Object Explorer connections and each query's server, database and attachment are restored after a restart or reload, and previously connected servers reconnect in the background unless you disconnected them. Background reconnect never opens a browser sign-in or runs query text. Disconnected servers stay in Object Explorer, and Disconnect asks whether to keep or close the server's query tabs.

changes.title: Getting Started, About and release notes
changes.text: Read offline guides to connecting, querying and results, with your current shortcuts and interactive fictional examples. About Varia shows the version, platform and update status, and Release Notes shows these highlights for the installed version or the one an update offers.

changes.title: Editor conveniences
changes.text: Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel to resize the editor font. New Query with sp_help, sp_who and sp_lock in the command palette stand in for SSMS's query shortcuts. Query tabs show the file name on one line and environment and session badges on a second.

changes.title: Much larger results
changes.text: Results can now use a quarter of the computer's memory up to 16 GiB (it was 2 GiB), half of it for one query. Set your own Result memory limit or Maximum rows kept per execution in Tools › Options › Query Results; changes apply at once.

changes.title: Results take less memory
changes.text: A large result you are not looking at or using is compressed in the background, typically to a third or half of its size, so more results fit. Nothing is dropped or written to disk. A query that fills result memory first waits briefly while others are compressed to make room.

changes.title: Faster result operations
changes.text: Sorting, filtering, value lists, profiles, Pivots, Distinct Count, search and Compare are many times faster on large results and use several processor cores, shared fairly between operations running at once. Changing only the sort no longer recomputes the column profile.

changes.title: Transpose is a view
changes.text: Transpose now turns the same grid on its side instead of adding a result, costing no result memory and following its sort, filters and selection. Copy and Save Results As write what the transposed grid shows.

changes.title: New shortcuts for results
changes.text: Tabs is the default results layout. Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 (Cmd on macOS) now pick query tabs and results like a browser's tabs, instead of SSMS's query shortcuts, which are in the command palette.

changes.title: Lighter search and startup
changes.text: Search Objects holds up to about 2.4 times as many objects per megabyte, and Ctrl+Q searches the same index, finding objects whether or not Object Explorer has loaded them. Startup no longer starts IntelliSense for the untouched welcome query, saving about 110 MB until your first edit.

changes.title: Updated runtime and components
changes.text: The SQL backend runs on .NET 11, shipped with Varia, so there is nothing to install. Electron 45.3.2, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 7.1.2 and other components bring security and stability fixes.

changes.title: Safer object actions and connections
changes.text: Delete a database now refuses to run if a different database has taken its name since the dialog opened. Dependent documents such as Table Designer and Activity Monitor no longer follow a replacement connection by server name alone, and an edited session file cannot make startup sign in with Windows or Entra authentication unasked.

changes.title: Results you can rely on
changes.text: Save Results As JSON writes numbers with more than 15 significant digits as strings so other tools keep their digits. A running query that fills result memory says so at once, with Stop query. Compare handles results without key columns, the mouse wheel scrolls very large transposed grids, and result operations are refused cleanly when the computer is low on memory.

changes.title: Stability across platforms
changes.text: Execution timeouts on Linux and macOS stop queries on time, a busy Activity Monitor probe no longer reconnects every other live view, Linux updates no longer delete a newer download, and File › Open opens the files it can read when one cannot be read. Script As handles ledger objects on Azure SQL Database and targets Managed Instance's real engine version.

changes.title: Results stay in memory
changes.text: Results are never written to disk. Transposed views and Keep Selected Rows use at most 4,095 rows and say when rows are left out, and a result that fills its memory limit is truncated with an explanation.

changes.title: Some features depend on permissions
changes.text: Kill Process requires ALTER ANY CONNECTION and is never offered for Varia's own connections. Recent Expensive Queries reads the plan cache only while its pane is shown. Entra IntelliSense is not available yet.

changes.title: Unsigned builds
changes.text: Builds remain unsigned, and macOS builds are not notarized. Your operating system may ask you to confirm that you trust the application.
